findings.problem: After `apply phaseAt_regulator_eq_and_le_one`, all four hypothesis goals start with the same `intro ht; rw [he]`. Two of them then prove a contrapositive by hand: `apply le_of_not_gt; intro h; exact (not_le_of_gt ht) (hh.2.1.mpr h.le)`, and the same again with `hh.2.2.1`. These are only the contrapositives of the threshold iffs in `hh` (`τ_mid ≤ t ↔ V/2 ≤ v` and `τ_end ≤ t ↔ V ≤ v`). Spelling them out over 19 lines hides that each hypothesis follows directly from one component of `hh`.
findings.proposed_change:
Rewrite with `he` once on the main goal, then pass the four hypotheses straight to the lemma:
```lean
  dsimp only at hh ⊢
  rw [he]
  refine phaseAt_regulator_eq_and_le_one _ ω i (horder ω i) t κ β
    (sourceClockLevel κ (z i) (u₀ i)) (κ/4*(u₂ i-u₀ i)) hβ _ hactive
    hh.1.mp
    (fun ht => (not_le.mp (mt hh.2.1.mpr (not_le_of_gt ht))).le)
    hh.2.1.mp
    (fun ht => (not_le.mp (mt hh.2.2.1.mpr (not_le_of_gt ht))).le)
```
(`_` replaces `(S.Q t ω i)`, which is now `logLoewnerCoordinates (G ω) (z i) t` after the rewrite.)
findings.benefit: The four `rw [he]` calls become one, so it is clear that the substitution `S.Q = logLoewnerCoordinates` is made once for the whole statement. Each of `hstart`, `hbefore`, `hafter` and `hend` then appears next to the part of `hh` it comes from: the forward direction of an iff, or its contrapositive via `mt`. The order of the arguments matches the lemma's hypotheses, so the reader can match each phase boundary to its clock threshold without working through two hand-written proofs by contradiction. The same lemmas (`hh.*.mpr`, `not_le_of_gt`) are used, so nothing is hidden behind automation.
